newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia coal supply security an issue - Parer.
newsitem.headline: Australia coal supply security an issue - Parer.

text.p: The security of coal supplies was an issue for major importers in Asia, Australian Resources and Energy minister Warwick Parer told Reuters.
Coking coal customers in Korea and Japan had voiced concern about security of supply in the new high demand era, he said.
They had suggested that new customers should be treated as late comers, he said, indicating that traditional buyers wished to be supplied first.
From Australia's perspective, security of supply could translate to a re-emphasis on long term contracts and on minority equity positions in Australian coal mines by Asian customers, he said.
Parer said he expected greater use of long term contracts.
The Australian government had no objection to foreign investments by Asian customers in Australian mines, he said.
Responding to questions, Parer said he had no feeling yet for the direction of current Australia-Japan coal negotiations in Tokyo.
"The Australian government always wants a price rise," he said, but would not predict results.
